premise: Keaton risked his life during the filming of Steamboat Bill, Jr. by standing in the exact spot where a real two-ton building wall dropped over him.
hook: A single misplaced step of two inches would have crushed him instantly, yet he insisted on doing the stunt without a double or trick camera.
key_facts: Filmed the climax of 'Steamboat Bill, Jr.' in 1928 during personal and financial distress.
Used a genuine building facade weighing an estimated two tons.
Cleared the falling frame through a single second-story window opening with only inches of tolerance.
Refused a stunt double and performed the sequence in a single continuous take.
